subject: Capacity Quickstart: Close timeline & pool-sizing proposal
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Amit Shah <amit@skyward.ai>, Lena Park <lena.park@skyward.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Capacity Quickstart: proposal and suggested MAP checkpoints

Hi Amit / Lena —

Thanks again for the conversation this morning. Per our notes, I pulled together a recommended capacity plan and a proposed mutual action plan (MAP) to get Skyward from eval -> committed Dedicated or Private deployment with predictable lead times. Attached is a short workbook (capacity_proposal_v2.xlsx) and a MAP SOW draft.

High-level recommendation (short):
- Target: 4x H100 reserved nodes (baseline) with the option to burst to 8x H100 for peak evaluation weeks.
- Typical throughput (estimate): ~200–300 tokens/s per H100 depending on model/seq length; we modeled a 50% concurrency buffer for production.
- Evaluation footprint: 1 reserved H100 + burst access to 2 additional nodes for a 4-week eval window.

Lead-times and expectations:
- Hosted/Dedicated (Redwood-managed): 6 weeks to provision from signed PO (hardware allocation + network config).
- Private (customer VPC or on-prem): 12–16 weeks (order, rack staging, network, and compliance runbook).
- Temporary burst windows (short-term capacity) can be enabled during evaluation to shorten perceived lead time while procurement completes.

Suggested MAP checkpoints (timeline sample):
1) Week 0 (this week): Agree on evaluation objectives, sign MAP SOW (high level), exchange SOC2 / data-residency checklist.
2) Weeks 1–4: Evaluation window (tech validation, perf baselines, prompt & eval harness).
3) Week 3: Procurement readiness review — procurement team drafts PO language; legal begins commercial review.
4) Week 4–6: Decision milestone — sign PO to lock Dedicated baseline; provisioning starts upon PO.

Mutual action items (first pass):
- Skyward: confirm primary models and sample prompt set for perf tests (due Tue).
- Redwood: provide evaluation pool reservation and a short runbook for network access (by Wed).
- Both: finalize MAP SOW draft comments (by EOW).

I attached the workbook and MAP SOW draft that map the above to concrete milestones and acceptance criteria. If you want, Karthik can drop in a brief sizing note to justify the pool numbers.

Next steps: can we lock a 30-minute MAP walk-through on Thu 10am PT to align on acceptance criteria and procurement asks?

Best,
Logan

Subject: Re: Capacity Quickstart: proposal and suggested MAP checkpoints

Logan —

Thanks for the clear summary. A few quick clarifying questions before we book the walkthrough:

1) SOC2 / compliance: our security team needs to see specific evidence for audit scope (audit dates, in-scope controls, evidence of log retention). Is Redwood willing to add SOC2 evidence as a MAP milestone before PO?
2) Burst / short-term capacity: can we get a firm SLA on burst availability during the eval window? If our eval spikes, we need guaranteed capacity or transparent throttling.
3) Pool sizing: the 4x H100 baseline looks reasonable — curious if you have a mid-point option (e.g., 2x reserved + burst to 6x) to lower the initial commit cost.

Procurement note: our internal PO cycles are usually 2–3 weeks after signatures and legal sign-off. We are trying to compress to 7–10 business days if Redwood can accept a provisional PO and invoice milestone.

I'll loop in our security lead if needed. Thu 10am PT works for the walkthrough.

— Amit
Amit Shah
Head of Product, Skyward AI
amit@skyward.ai
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Amit Shah <amit@skyward.ai>, Lena Park <lena.park@skyward.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-30T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity Quickstart: proposal and suggested MAP checkpoints

Amit — thanks for the questions, good ones. Short answers and commitments below.

1) SOC2 / evidence: yes — we can include a SOC2 evidence bundle as an item in the MAP (Milestone A). We typically provide the SOC2 report, a short evidence index, and a transient read-only access to a redacted audit evidence folder for procurement review. Estimated delivery: 3 business days after you request milestone A.

2) Burst SLA during eval: we can offer a burst reservation with a 99th-percentile availability target for the evaluation window. The way we operationalize this is: reserved baseline + committed burst pool with pre-wired capacity in our scheduler. If you choose the provisional PO route, we can convert temporary burst capacity to committed nodes faster. I'll have Marissa include a one-page note on expected availability and throttling behavior in the MAP SOW.

3) Mid-point option: absolutely — two practical options:
  - Option A (lower commit): 2x reserved H100 baseline + ability to burst to 6x (recommended if you want lower TCO initially).
  - Option B (higher performance): 4x reserved H100 baseline + burst to 8x.

I attached an updated swimlane in the MAP SOW (MAP_SOW_draft_20270529.pdf) that maps these choices to PO timing and provisioning windows.

Walkthrough confirmed for Thu 10am PT — I'll send the calendar invite and a short slide (5m) to ground the meeting.

Best,
Logan

Amit — adding a brief technical note on sizing and what to expect during the eval so procurement/security have concrete numbers for capacity planning.

Sizing rationale (concise):
- Baseline unit: H100 (80GB) chosen for memory headroom on models in your list and for more efficient KV cache usage.
- Per-node perf: we benchmarked ~220 tokens/sec for 512-token sequences on our 70B-style models in real-world prompt mixes; smaller models will be proportionally faster.
- Concurrency planning: fair-share scheduler will allocate CPU/NIC resources to allow ~40–60 concurrent sessions per H100 before queuing behavior increases latency beyond the MAP acceptance target.

Operational points:
- Monitoring & alerting: we will provide token-level cost and latency dashboards (console link in MAP SOW) and a tracer you can use to correlate slow requests.
- Acceptance criteria for eval: 95th percentile gen latency < 350ms for small prompts and validated functional throughput for your three representative workloads.

If you prefer, we can prepare a short perf-run script for your environment to reproduce the numbers during the walkthrough.

— Karthik

Logan / Karthik —

Appreciate the notes and the sizing detail. We reviewed the MAP SOW and the procurement team confirmed they can aim for a provisional PO within 7 business days once we sign the MAP. Our security team also confirmed the SOC2 evidence approach should be acceptable.

Decision summary:
- We will proceed with Option A (2x reserved H100, burst to 6x) for the initial commitment.
- MAP acceptance criteria agreed as per Karthik's note; security milestone A for SOC2 evidence is required prior to provisioning.
- Procurement will issue provisional PO by 2027-06-11 and expects final invoicing after provisioning.

Can you add a short procurement checklist (PO language sample) in the MAP SOW so our procurement team can expedite? Also please include expected billing milestones tied to provisioning events.

I'll mark the deal as green on our side and loop our legal if we need redlines. Thanks — looking forward to the walkthrough on Thu.

— Amit
